The producer narrowed the decision rule to 'positive control only for passing measure' and omitted null-control-at-all-n — both contradict the frozen spec and cannot be applied post-hoc. The measurand is also shifted: KDE computed without permutation mean subtraction (observed BC, not frozen BC = max(0, observed - perm_mean)) and kNN uses simplified neighbor-count estimator (run_execute.py:93-111) not the preregistered Kraskov k=5 estimator. These violations make the producer's metrics non-comparable to parent baselines and to the frozen CV<=0.5 criterion. The audit correctly identifies this as measurement invalidity, not a scientific negative. The hypothesis that per-type CV stability scales to 500-1000/type remains untested under valid measurement.
